title: Epochal Rewrite Controller and KV Fragmentation Heatmap
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Implement an "epochal" rewrite controller for the KV cache that reduces long-lived fragmentation by periodically identifying high-fragmentation segments and proactively rewriting live entries into compact regions. Complement this with a lightweight fragmentation heatmap telemetry feature that runs on-host (not on-GPU) to surface allocation hotspots, wasted bytes, and temporal churn patterns to the Console. The goal is to reduce GPU memory tail fragmentation, improve steady-state utilization, and keep latency regressions within SLO during continuous batching scenarios.

Why this work now:
- Continuous batching increases the residency time of KV entries, which exacerbates external/internal fragmentation over long steady states.
- Existing background compaction is reactive and bursts at high cost; we want a predictable, low-latency approach that works in concert with batching.
- Customers running Dedicated/Private clusters have reported gradual GPU memory pressure and OOM events during high-concurrency tails.

Goals and non-goals:
- Goals:
  - Keep fragmentation ratio (wasted bytes / total KV bytes) below 6% on long-running workloads (>72h) for sampled clusters.
  - Limit additional p50/p95 generation latency to <5% when rewrite operations run concurrently with normal inference.
  - Provide heatmap telemetry in Console showing per-region fragmentation score, rewrite throughput, and success/failure rates.
- Non-goals:
  - This ticket does not change the allocator internals (no slab redesign). It orchestrates rewrites and adds telemetry and placement hints for future allocator work.

Design overview:
1) Fragmentation heatmap (host-side):
   - Periodic sampler collects allocation metadata: allocation size class, slot density, last-access epoch, and free hole lengths per region.
   - Computes a per-region fragmentation score: frag_score = alpha * hole_ratio + beta * cold_live_ratio + gamma * churn_rate. Tunable weights, default alpha=0.6,beta=0.3,gamma=0.1.
   - Emits aggregated telemetry to Console via the existing runtime metrics pipeline; sample rate is low (1/min by default) and rate-limited per-instance.

2) Epochal rewrite controller (on-host orchestrator):
   - Runs a soft-pass every N epochs (epoch = configurable window aligned to continuous batching boundaries, default 20s).
   - Selects candidate regions with frag_score above threshold AND with a minimum reclaimable bytes estimate.
   - For each candidate, schedules small bounded rewrite jobs that: read live entries from GPU memory, pack them into contiguous destination region(s), update indirection/metadata, and release source slots.
   - Write jobs are micro-batched to align with inference batching patterns to avoid disrupting steady-state batching efficiency.
   - Controller respects backpressure signals from the serving runtime (active_request_count, burst_window) and pauses/backs off when latency SLOs are under pressure.

Implementation notes:
- Use existing copy/evict APIs for moving entries; add an idempotent "move with CAS" helper to avoid races (read-check-copy-update metadata in a single host transaction).
- Destination allocation should prefer contiguous free spans; if contiguous spans are unavailable, pack into the smallest number of spans up to a configurable max_spans_per_move.
- Maintain a small in-memory rewrite journal for in-flight moves to allow crash recovery and avoid orphaned indirections. Journal entries are compact and flushed to existing durable logs used by node agents.
- Integrate heatmap metrics with Console dashboards; add an annotation in the per-model runtime view showing "fragmentation risk".

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit and integration tests for move helper show correctness under simulated races.
- Performance test harness (scale test) shows fragmentation ratio drop >=40% relative to baseline after 48h of synthetic continuous-batch workload and no >5% p95 latency regression.
- Heatmap telemetry visible in Console dev environment with correct mapping to regions and ability to surface top-3 hotspot regions.
- Rollout plan documented and kill-switch available (feature flag + runtime pause endpoint).

Telemetry and observability:
- New metrics: kv_fragmentation_score_by_region, kv_rewrite_moves_total, kv_rewrite_bytes_moved, kv_rewrite_failures_total, kv_rewrite_pause_duration_seconds.
- Tracing: annotate rewrite jobs with trace id linking to copy operations and allocation updates.
- Alerting: add an alert when avg frag_score > 0.15 for >30m on a node in production (thresholds TBD after initial rollout).

Rollout plan:
1) Canary: enable on 1 Dedicated node in staging with feature flag; monitor metrics and collect traces for 72h.
2) Gradual ramp: 5% of nodes for 1w, 25% for next 2w.
3) Full rollout if no regressions and fragmentation reduces per acceptance criteria.
4) In case of regressions, immediate rollback via feature flag and runtime pause.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for frag_score computation over synthetic allocation maps.
- Integration e2e in perf harness with continuous batching generator; measure fragmentation and latency delta.
- Fault injection: mid-move node crash and ensure journal-driven recovery corrects indirections.
- Safety: validate move operation is idempotent under duplicated requests.

Risks and mitigation:
- Race with live inference touching KV entries: mitigate using CAS-style metadata updates and short-lived read-locks.
- Unexpected latency spikes during aggressive rewriting: use adaptive backoff and limit rewrite concurrency to a fraction of CPU/GPU bandwidth.
- Incorrect telemetry causing false positives: start with conservative sampling and allow tuning in-console.

Open questions:
- Should we expose frag_score tuning to tenants on Dedicated clusters? (Pros: faster mitigation for critical tenants; Cons: complexity/abuse)
- Default epoch window for continuous batching alignment; recommended starting value is 20s but needs validation.
